A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Langevin-convergence research. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original sampling experiments on one-, two- and ten-dimensional Gaussian mixtures.

after.justification: The Gaussian-mixture experiments remain, with additional fixed-step comparisons and original image-denoising results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The Langevin diffusion, Euler–Maruyama update, four annealing paths and posterior-path construction remain the same. The learned prior used in the new imaging experiment does not establish a revision of the sampling procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only synthetic Gaussian mixtures in dimensions 1, 2 and 10. v2 retains these and adds posterior sampling for denoising a 256-by-256 CelebA image with Gaussian corruption and a learned prior, substantially extending task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: Matched Gaussian-mixture comparisons retain ULA, dilation, geometric tempering, convolution and DAZ. The new denoising experiment uses existing comparators and excludes DAZ because of proximal-operator difficulties; no comparator is removed from a retained experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a controlled comparison using the same constant step h=a0/L0² for every path, alongside the retained path-dependent steps. The new denoising protocol uses h=0.001, noise standard deviation 0.5, initialization at the noisy image, and MSE against a 30,000-iteration ULA reference.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 examines physical time accumulated under different step sizes. Appendix A.3 and Figure 4 add a focused equal-step ablation testing whether annealing benefits persist independently of larger allowable steps. Existing schedule-sensitivity and mode-coverage analyses remain.

E5.justification: For denoising, Figure 8 newly defines a Monte Carlo posterior-mean estimator using 50 samples with thinning interval 10. This adds an estimation procedure, not repeated-seed uncertainty analysis. The Gaussian-mixture use of 5,000 independent chains remains, without new confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained Gaussian-mixture curves and histograms change, including the ten-dimensional trajectories in v1 Figure 5 versus v2 Figure 7. v2 also adds equal-step KL results, step-size diagnostics, denoising images and MSE trajectories. These are revised and additional outcomes; unspecified random realizations prevent interpreting the changed synthetic curves as demonstrated same-instance performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit uniform log-Sobolev assumption, worst-case complexity statements and derivations for Theorems 4.4 and 4.7, and the constant-bound derivation in Lemma B.6. It also adds the missing Lipschitz hypothesis to the DAZ proposition, changes Equation (16) from equality to an upper bound, and revises the partition-function proof.

C1.justification: Path-design guidance becomes an explicit contribution and is refined into recommendations involving the dissipativity and Lipschitz parameters. v1 already offered qualitative guidance, so this is a limited refinement. The abstract and principal claims about unified forward-KL convergence and covered paths remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits the theory to smooth potentials, discusses the difficulty of selecting optimal schedules, and qualifies the denoising metric and learned-prior assumptions. It also connects path benefits more specifically to parameter bounds and corrects the guidance from larger to smaller log-Sobolev constants.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 supplies explicit parameter-estimation and step-size formulas for all compared schemes. Appendix A.6 identifies the DiffUNet prior from DeepInverse and specifies image corruption, initialization, step size and posterior-mean estimation. These substantially expand documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments' underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on recent annealing and posterior sampling, including Cattiaux et al. (2025), Young et al. (2026), Xun et al. (2025) and Blumenthal et al. (2025), plus sources supporting the LSI derivation and imaging experiment. The central positioning and related-work discussion remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained. v2 edits terminology and prose, separates the practical remarks, expands appendix organization, and updates affiliations and conference front matter. The added scientific material does not amount to a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds four substantive displays: physical-time plots, equal-step KL plots, an image-denoising grid and denoising MSE curves. Retained figures are renumbered or relocated, including the two-dimensional image grid moving to a dedicated page. The visual expansion goes substantially beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The equal-step control, imaging example, explicit assumptions and implementation details improve evidential coverage and transparency. However, new technical material contains internal inconsistencies: Equation (41) gives L_tau=0 when tau>1/L0, making the stated step rule undefined, and Lemma B.6 differentiates exp(-alpha|x|²) with the wrong sign. The PDFs do not resolve whether these are transcription errors or affect the implementation and guarantees. These competing gains and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
